raw_segments.text: Cleopatra. That time?—O times!—I laughed him out of patience, and that night I laughed
him into patience, and next morn, Ere the ninth hour, I drunk him to his bed, Then put
my tires and mantles on him, whilst I wore his sword Philippan.
Cleopatra, That time, O times, I laughed him out of patience,
And that night I laughed him into patience, And next morn, ere the ninth hour,
I drunk him to his bed, Then put my tires and mantles on him,
Whilst I wore his sword, Philippan.
Cleopatra, that time—oh, times—I laughed him out of patience.
And that night I laughed him into patience, and next morning, ere the ninth hour, I drunk
him to his bed, then put my tires and mantles on him, whilst I wore his sword, Philippan.
